name: PRISMA
tagline: Dutch research prototype (1986-1991) of a parallel, main-memory relational DBMS; a MonetDB ancestor.
description: PRISMA/DB was the database half of PRISMA, a Dutch national research project run by CWI, the University of Twente and Philips Research in the late 1980s. It was one of the earliest attempts at a shared-nothing, parallel relational DBMS that kept all data in main memory, with each fragment of a relation managed by its own process on a multi-node machine and queries executed with intra- and inter-operator parallelism. Results were published through 1992 in IEEE TKDE and elsewhere, and the CWI team around Martin Kersten later built MonetDB on lessons from it. It never shipped as a product and is now of interest only for the history of parallel and in-memory databases.
statusNote: Research prototype (1986-1991); never released as a product. Its in-memory, parallel ideas carried into MonetDB.
developer: CWI, University of Twente and Philips Research

scale.notes: Data fragmented across the nodes of a single parallel machine; sized by that machine's total memory.

strengths: Early demonstration of a shared-nothing parallel relational engine
Kept all relations in main memory years before in-memory databases were commercial
Direct intellectual ancestor of CWI's MonetDB
weaknesses: Never released; no code or binaries are publicly available
Tied to custom research hardware and languages of its era
useCases: Studying the history of parallel and main-memory databases
Background reading for database systems courses
notIdealFor: Any practical workload: there is nothing to install
